product_one_liner.value: Together AI provides a cloud platform for AI engineers and researchers to build, fine-tune, and deploy open-source AI models using inference services and GPU clusters.
product_one_liner.notes: The company describes its audience as AI engineers and researchers and its product as a unified platform for building, fine-tuning and deploying open-source models with inference and GPU clusters: https://linkedin.com/company/togethercomputer and https://www.together.ai/products.

pricing_page.notes: A public pricing page describes pricing for serverless inference, dedicated endpoints, fine-tuning and GPU clusters: https://www.together.ai/pricing.

eng_blog.notes: The research index identifies technical and engineering content: https://www.together.ai/research-blog?1ed7628f_page=19. Two substantive examples are FlashAttention, covering GPU-memory IO complexity and attention implementation (https://www.together.ai/blog/flashattentionfandm), and FlexGen, covering an inference engine's memory architecture and linking its implementation (https://www.together.ai/blog/flexgen-high-throughput-generative-inference-of-large-language-models-with-a-single-gpu). These are authored technical research and engineering contributions rather than marketing posts; the engineering-author characterization is based on their technical contributions rather than explicit job titles.

public_docs.notes: The public documentation overview exposes multiple guides, including running models, launching GPU clusters and building agents: http://docs.together.ai/.

ai_ml_roles_open.notes: The live job posting and company job board list Machine Learning Engineer - Inference, a qualifying ML role: https://job-boards.greenhouse.io/togetherai/jobs/4385540007 and https://job-boards.greenhouse.io/togetherai?page=2.

model_provider.value: Llama and Qwen models, served through Together AI's inference platform.
model_provider.notes: The enterprise page explicitly says customers can run Llama or Qwen on the Together Inference Engine: https://www.together.ai/enterprise. This identifies supported models without implying an undisclosed external model-provider dependency.
